title: Re Sean Ozbalt and Re Erin Barr v. Pacific Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained Case 2020-09 and answered it by reference to the consolidated decision, which annulled the minister’s deposition. No specifications were separately denied. The SJC recommended treating the elapsed 17 months as definite suspension and closing the matter; it did not annul dissolution of the minister’s call.
first_summary: Pacific Crossroads Church’s Session challenged Presbytery’s use of an adverse investigative report outside a minister’s agreed BCO 38-1 confession before deposing him. The SJC sustained the complaint by reference to its consolidated decision, holding that the additional material prejudiced the accused and violated BCO 38-1. It annulled the deposition and recommended treating the minister’s elapsed 17 months under censure as definite suspension and closing the matter.
summary: Pacific Crossroads Church’s Session challenged Presbytery’s handling of a minister’s BCO 38-1 confession, particularly its hearing an adverse investigative report outside the agreed statement before imposing deposition. The SJC sustained Case 2020-09 by reference to its consolidated decision and annulled the deposition: BCO 38-1 permits censure to rest only on the mutually approved statement, not additional adverse material. It recommended treating the elapsed 17 months as definite suspension and closing the matter. The minister returned to good standing without call; dissolution of his call remained intact.
